solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sit oddly posed, captured by rhythmically precise French painter

indicators.note: posed in an odd way means the letters are set out in a new arrangement
something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: keeping exactly to the beat is being 'in time'
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist sits awkwardly for a portrait painted with metronomic exactness by a French painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged SIT goes inside IN TIME, between its M and final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimiste is a French painter of intimate domestic interiors, such as Vuillard or Bonnard.

clue.text: Clip joint? Money raised before installing one

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts its letters upward so it reads from bottom to top
to install something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: tin is slang for money
ere is an old word for before
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dodgy club charges money up front once someone has been let in.
explanation.walkthrough: A clip joint is a club that overcharges its customers; the question mark flags that a niterie (nightclub) need not be one.
explanation.definitionFit: A niterie is a nightclub, and a clip joint is a sleazy nightclub that fleeces its patrons, so this is an example.

clue.text: Organ device tool adjusted, introducing rapid movement of a kind

indicators.note: adjusting something alters its arrangement, so these letters are reordered
introducing means bringing something in, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
REM is rapid eye movement, the kind of movement during dreaming sleep

explanation.surface: An organ builder adjusts a tool and sets something moving fast inside the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rapid movement of a kind' is the sleep term rapid eye movement, abbreviated; 'Organ device' could mislead toward body organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is the organ stop or mechanism that makes the sound waver rapidly in volume.

clue.text: Lives for ever? That's surprising (4, two words)

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist, so 'lives' is IS
ay (aye) is an old word meaning always, for ever

explanation.surface: Someone hears a person will live for ever and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: AY in the sense 'ever, always' is the poetic word seen in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses mild astonishment, just as a remark of 'That's surprising' would.

clue.text: Small freshwater fish, otherwise found under the sea

indicators.note: in a down entry something found under another sits below it, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
aka, also known as, introduces another name

explanation.surface: A tiny freshwater fish has turned up, against expectation, on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'found under' places the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The medaka is a small Japanese freshwater fish, the rice fish, popular in aquariums and laboratories.

clue.text: Female eagles heading south for Medway location

blocks.note: a female is a she
an erne is a sea eagle
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Female eagles head south to the Medway estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' places the south abbreviation at the end. The Medway is a river in Kent, south-east England, whose mouth Sheerness overlooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a port town on the Isle of Sheppey at the mouth of the River Medway.

clue.text: Pigeon, disordered but not dead, on time

indicators.note: 'but not' means except for, so something is left out of the preceding word

blocks.note: turbid means muddled or disordered
D is the abbreviation for dead
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bewildered pigeon, still alive, turns up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disordered' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym for TURBID, which loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbit is a breed of domestic fancy pigeon with a short beak and a frill of feathers on the breast.

clue.text: Conifer coloured unfenced garden, variegated

indicators.note: without its fence a plot loses its boundary, so the outer letters go and the inside stays
variegated means patterned in varied ways, so these letters are set out differently

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for coloured
the inside letters of garden

explanation.surface: A conifer with coloured foliage stands in an open, multicoloured garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a tall evergreen tree bearing cones, so it is one of the conifers.

clue.text: Tumour in part of anatomy (omasum)

indicators.note: the answer is found within a part of the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A growth is found in part of a cow's anatomy, the omasum or third stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The omasum is a ruminant's third stomach, which makes the surface sound like a vet's report.
explanation.definitionFit: A myoma is a benign tumour made of muscle tissue, such as a fibroid.

clue.text: Foster-mother abroad, mobile, given rations permit

blocks.note: M is an abbreviation for mobile, as for a mobile phone number
an etape is a military ration or allowance of food on a march
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A foster-mother overseas, always on the move, is issued with food rations and a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: ETAPE (from the French étape) is a rare Chambers word for a soldier's daily rations.
explanation.definitionFit: A metapelet is the Hebrew name for a woman who looked after the children on an Israeli kibbutz, hence a foster-mother abroad.

clue.text: Ribes growing wild in part of Jock's stubble

indicators.note: something growing wild runs out of order, so these letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the botanical name for currants

explanation.surface: Currant bushes sprout untamed in a Scotsman's bristly chin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ribes is the currant genus; Jock is the crossword's Scotsman, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Birse is Scots for a bristle, so a single hair of a Scotsman's stubble.

clue.text: Sleep that's rapid coming upon the old

indicators.note: coming upon means arriving on top of, so in this across entry the first piece is set before the second

blocks.note: a shute (chute) is a rapid, a steep fall of water in a river; rapid is a noun here
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: An elderly person drops off to sleep quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rapid' reads as an adjective but is a noun, a stretch of fast water. 'coming upon' puts it before the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is the informal word for sleep, from closing the eyes.

clue.text: Not quite sober? Help as before needed

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: steady can mean sober and temperate

explanation.surface: Someone a little the worse for drink asks for the help they needed before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks an archaic sense: stead once meant to help or be of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead is an obsolete verb meaning to help or avail, as in 'it steads me nothing'.

clue.text: Jeweller's stone, unconcealed, I provide as inset

indicators.note: an inset is set into something else, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: pert is an old word meaning open or unconcealed
I plus DO, to do being to provide, as in 'we do lunches'

explanation.surface: A jeweller openly offers to supply a stone as an inset piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic sense of pert, meaning open or evident, is the one used here; 'I provide' is read as a little sentence, I do.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of olivine used in jewellery.

clue.text: What'll attract attention and stifle news just breaking

blocks.note: st! is an interjection used to catch someone's attention
to oppress is to stifle or weigh down

explanation.surface: A newsroom wonders how to grab attention and suppress a breaking story.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests a cryptic definition of a headline, but it splits into a call for attention plus a word for stifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is late news inserted into a paper after printing has begun, so it is news just breaking.

clue.text: Body measurement

blocks.note: read plainly: a measurement taken round part of the body
the setter's reading is the same: this is a bare definition with no wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition word: it is given only a plain definition, and readers send in their own cryptic clues for it, so there is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistline is the girth around the narrowest part of the trunk, measured for clothing.

clue.text: Intrinsic part of erotica, mainly?

indicators.note: an intrinsic part lies within the whole, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asks what forms the essential core of most erotic material.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay hides the answer; with the question mark the same words also hint at what erotica is mostly about.
explanation.definitionFit: Cama (Kama) is earthly desire, or the Hindu god of love, which is plausibly the main substance of erotica.

clue.text: Skill backing with bloke on board horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for skill reads from right to left
someone on board is inside the vessel, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: art is skill
oik is British slang for an uncouth bloke

explanation.surface: A skilled driver reverses a carriage with a man aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: OIK, a common British insult for a boorish or lower-class man, goes between the T R and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sledge drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Wretched nag having to carry away old foundation material

blocks.note: a rip is a worthless horse
rap is an obsolete verb meaning to snatch or carry away

explanation.surface: A miserable old horse is made to haul away ancient building material.
explanation.definitionFit: Riprap is loose broken stone thrown down to form a foundation or protect an embankment.

clue.text: A pointilliste may spatter tile with these

definitions.text: A pointilliste may spatter tile with these

indicators.note: spattering scatters things about, so the letters on either side are scrambled into each other

blocks.note: taken as written: the full pool of letters
taken as written: these letters are part of the pool and are set aside

explanation.surface: A pointillist painter might dab a tile with these colours.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of A POINTILLISTE rearrange into TILE plus the answer, so take TILE away and what remains is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointillist painters such as Seurat worked in oils, applying the colour in small dots.

clue.text: Nutritional component in wine cheers artery

indicators.note: the words before sit inside the wine word, which wraps around them

blocks.note: vin is French for wine
ta is British informal thanks
the M1 is the main motorway artery north from London, M plus 1 as I

explanation.surface: A dietary element in wine is toasted for its good effect on the arteries.
explanation.walkthrough: An artery is a main road, and the M1 is Britain's first motorway, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin is an organic compound needed in small amounts in the diet, so a nutritional component.

clue.text: Partner, single, in Italian ball game

blocks.note: a pal is a mate or partner
lone means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A partner and a solo player take part in an Italian ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallone is an old Italian game in which a large ball is struck with a wooden guard worn on the arm.

clue.text: Sob freely, fit when interring one — in such …

definitions.note: the definition runs on into the next clue: 'in such funeral rites', an adjective phrase

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so these letters move into any order
interring means burying, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
fit as in equal to a task
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mourners weep openly at a burial, and it is fitting, at such a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence into the next clue, so the definition here reads together with its 'Funeral rites'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequial means relating to obsequies, which are funeral rites.

clue.text: Sharp turn fastening cable

blocks.note: first meaning: acrid or harsh in taste
second meaning: a nautical turn of a cable round the bitts on deck

explanation.surface: A tight twist secures a ship's rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The bitts are a pair of posts on a ship's deck; a turn of cable around them is a bitter, whence 'the bitter end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a sharp, acrid taste and a nautical noun for a turn of cable round posts.

clue.text: The old move to crouch low removing cap before church

indicators.note: in a down entry the cap is the top, so the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: to squat is to crouch low
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An old person bends low, doffing a hat, before entering church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word: quatch is a variant of a Spenserian verb meaning to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Quatch is an obsolete verb meaning to move or stir, so it suits 'The old move'.

clue.text: … Funeral rites, led by priest? Statistician's unit

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front, so the second-named piece comes first in the answer

blocks.note: PR is an abbreviation for priest
obit is an old word for funeral rites or a memorial service

explanation.surface: A priest leads the funeral; then a statistician steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by' puts the priest first. The opening words also finish the previous clue's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A probit is a unit used in statistics, a probability transformed via the normal distribution.

clue.text: What stationer stocks: rubber for use in centre of carrel

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the innermost letters are kept
to be used in something is to be put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the two letters at the heart of carrel
ule is a Central American rubber tree

explanation.surface: A stationer keeps erasers in stock for use in library study cubicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' suggests an eraser but is ULE, a rubber tree; a carrel is a study cubicle in a library.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler for drawing lines is part of any stationer's stock, so it is an example.

clue.text: Brave, perhaps, ignoring first bit of medicine?

indicators.note: ignoring the first letter means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: a dosage is a measured portion of a medicine

explanation.surface: Is it brave to skip the first spoonful of medicine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is the noun for a Native American warrior, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people, so an Osage warrior is an example of a brave.

clue.text: Sell stores to soldiers, crafty as of old

blocks.note: first meaning: to act as a sutler, a camp provisioner
second meaning: an obsolete spelling of subtle, cunning

explanation.surface: An old-time army trader cunningly sells supplies to the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Suttle is a verb for trading as a sutler with an army, and also an archaic form of subtle, meaning cunning.

clue.text: Druggie's back to front dodge

indicators.note: the back letter is taken round to the front of the word

blocks.note: a user is a drug-taker; the 's is just 'has'

explanation.surface: An addict turns round to pull a fast one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves only the last letter, not the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem, which is what a dodge is.

clue.text: Ballet character, cunning, escaping home of fabled monster

indicators.note: something escaping gets out, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: wiliness is cunning
Loch Ness is the home of the Loch Ness monster

explanation.surface: A dancer cleverly flees the lair of a legendary beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' reads as an adjective but is the noun, WILINESS.

clue.text: Protein in e.g. tendons entails flexing

indicators.note: flexing bends and moves things about, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Bending a tendon involves a protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the elastic fibrous protein found in connective tissue such as tendons, ligaments and arteries.

clue.text: Misanthrope making money in a jiffy? The opposite

indicators.note: this swaps the order of the 'in' just stated, so the outer and inner pieces trade places

blocks.note: tin is slang for money
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A cynic makes a fast buck, then wonders about the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'money in a jiffy', but 'The opposite' flips it: the jiffy goes inside the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, the title character of Shakespeare's play, became the archetypal hater of mankind.

clue.text: Divide up FBI agents in group

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the word for group

blocks.note: a set is a group
G-men are FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents split a gang into factions.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to divide it into separate parts.

clue.text: Nick, college joiner

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for college
a link joins things

explanation.surface: A man called Nick works as a college carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is British slang for prison, as is clink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nick and clink are British slang terms for a prison.

clue.text: Brain surgeon, maybe, reverse of brisk in cutting into this lady

indicators.note: the reverse of a word reads it backwards, right to left
cutting into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: pert means lively or brisk
her refers to this lady
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brisk brain surgeon operates on a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'in' is itself a piece that goes inside HER, while 'cutting into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trephiner bores holes in the skull with a trephine, as a brain surgeon might.
